title: Why Sharp Things Work
description: Armed with the pressure formula, spot the Baron's weak points. Sharp, thin, pointed — that's where pressure wins.

content.value: A knife's sharp edge, a needle's point, and a nail's tip all have a very SMALL area. Push with an ordinary force and, because the area is tiny, the pressure becomes huge — enough to cut, pierce, or sink in.

SHARP (small area → high pressure)   WIDE (large area → low pressure)
🔪  knife cuts easily                🛷  wide skis stop you sinking in snow
📌  pin pierces board                🐫  camel's broad feet on sand
💉  needle enters skin               🎒  wide straps don't dig into shoulders

Sometimes we WANT low pressure. Skis and snowshoes have a large area so your weight is spread out — you glide instead of sinking into the snow. A camel's wide feet stop it sinking into desert sand. Wide straps on a heavy bag spread the force so they don't dig into your shoulders.
Tall buildings have wide foundations so their enormous weight is spread over a large area of ground, giving low pressure so they don't sink. This is pressure engineering all around us.
Ask yourself: 'Do I want it to sink in or stay on top?' Sink in → make it sharp (small area). Stay on top → make it wide (large area).
Key Takeaway: Small areas create high pressure (knives, needles, nails cut and pierce). Large areas create low pressure (skis, camel feet, wide foundations spread out weight).

quiz.question: A sharp knife cuts better than a blunt one because its thin edge…
options: has a smaller area, giving higher pressure
quiz.explain: The tiny area of a sharp edge produces very high pressure for the same force, so it cuts easily.

quiz.question: Why do skis help you move over snow without sinking?
options: Their large area spreads your weight, lowering the pressure
They increase the pressure on the snow
quiz.explain: The large ski area spreads your weight over more snow, giving low pressure so you don't sink.

quiz.question: A camel's broad feet are an example of using a large area to…
options: reduce pressure so it doesn't sink into sand
quiz.explain: Wide feet spread the camel's weight over a big area, lowering pressure on the loose sand.
